findings.title: Client-side rendering gap: raw HTML contains minimal text content
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.frontiersin.org/people/login?returnUrl=http%3a%2f%2finternal-myfrontiers.frontiersin.org%2fmy-frontiers%2foverview via static_initial_html_shell_inspection [2026-09-13T16:34:09Z]: Raw HTML yields only 7 words of visible text and shows static shell signals (very-low-readable-text, markup-to-text-imbalance). Search crawlers and AI bots that do not execute client JS may not extract brand facts from this page. Other page-level checks were suppressed here: a missing heading, CTA, meta description or schema on an empty shell are all symptoms of this one root cause. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Implement server-side rendering (SSR) or static pre-rendering for core content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Use static site generation (SSG) or SSR so that primary textual facts and headers are present in initial HTTP responses without JS execution.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves render gap by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Missing Schema.org Organization structured data on root landing page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.frontiersin.org/ via jsonld_schema_extractor [2026-09-13T16:34:09Z]: Root homepage contains 0 Organization or LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema blocks. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add Organization JSON-LD markup to the homepage.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a JSON-LD script on the homepage declaring @type 'Organization' with name, url, logo, and sameAs links to authoritative profiles.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves structured data by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.
suggested_action.fix_snippet:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Frontiers",
  "url": "https://www.frontiersin.org",
  "logo": "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_LOGO_URL",
  "description": "Open access publisher of peer-reviewed scientific articles across the entire spectrum of academia. Research network for academics to stay up-to-date with the latest scientific publications, events, blogs and news.",
  "sameAs": [
    "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_WIKIPEDIA_OR_LINKEDIN_URL"
  ]
}
</script>

findings.title: Content images carry no text alternative, hiding any fact they display
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/science/article-hubs/circular-wastewater-treatment-solutions via image_alt_coverage_inspection [2026-09-13T16:34:09Z]: 12 of 22 images (55%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add descriptive alt text to every image that carries information.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Give each informational image an alt attribute stating the fact it conveys ("Pro plan: $49 per user per month"), not a filename. Mark purely decorative images with alt="" so they are correctly skipped rather than left unlabelled.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves fact extractability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: No site search affordance found on any crawled page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.frontiersin.org via search_affordance_detection [2026-09-13T16:34:09Z]: None of the 5 crawled pages expose a search input, a search form or role="search". A visitor who arrives on the wrong page from an AI answer has no way to find the right one without returning to the assistant. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Add a site search box to the persistent header.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a search input in the global header and expose it with role="search". Add WebSite JSON-LD with a potentialAction SearchAction so assistants can surface your search directly.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves navigation by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: No returning-visitor or account affordance detected
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.frontiersin.org via returning_visitor_affordance_detection [2026-09-13T16:34:09Z]: Across 5 crawled pages there is no sign-in, account, saved-items or recently-viewed affordance in the visible text. Every visitor is therefore treated as anonymous and first-time, so nothing the brand already knows about a returning visitor can shape what they are shown. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Give returning visitors a way to be recognised, and use it.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add an account or saved-state affordance appropriate to the site (sign-in, saved items, recently viewed, or a lightweight preference stored locally), then use it to surface relevant content on return rather than resetting every visitor to a cold start.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves personalization readiness by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

assessments.reason: robots.txt was fetched and its rules were applied to page and link fetches.
Initial HTML was inspected for shell signals; no browser rendering was used.
Answerability was checked against accessible on-site text and structured data only.
Only explicitly linked authority domains were inspected; external sources were not fabricated or searched.
No agent-supplied external discovery evidence was provided; no external search was performed.

proactive_recommendations.title: Mark up existing question-and-answer content with FAQPage schema
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already contains question-shaped content, but none of it is marked as FAQPage. FAQPage is the highest-leverage schema type for AI citation because its question/answer structure matches how retrieval systems chunk content and lift a quotable answer. The content already exists; only the markup is missing.

suggested_action.summary: Add FAQPage JSON-LD to pages that already answer common questions.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Wrap each question and its answer in FAQPage JSON-LD with mainEntity -> Question -> acceptedAnswer. Mark up the answers you already publish rather than writing new ones.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add Article schema with author and dateModified to editorial pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 2 crawled page(s) are editorial or documentation content carrying no Article schema. Authorship and a machine-readable modification date are the signals assistants use to decide whether a passage is current and attributable -- without them, an assistant that finds a good answer on the page still has no basis to date it or credit it.

suggested_action.summary: Mark editorial and documentation pages with Article JSON-LD.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Article or TechArticle JSON-LD with headline, author (a Person or Organization with a real profile URL), datePublished and dateModified. Update dateModified when the content genuinely changes, not on every deploy.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add BreadcrumbList schema to deep pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 4 crawled page(s) sit two or more levels deep with no BreadcrumbList markup. Breadcrumbs give both a visitor arriving cold from an AI answer and the assistant itself the parent context a deep URL otherwise lacks.

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD alongside visible breadcrumb navigation.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Emit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD listing each ancestor with position, name and item URL, and render the same trail visibly at the top of the page.

proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a Content Signals Policy block declaring your position on search, ai-input and ai-train separately, or publish RSL licensing terms. Keep it consistent with the agents you actually allow, or the two signals will contradict each other.

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose an agent-facing endpoint (NLWeb / MCP) built on existing structured data
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already publishes structured data, which is the input NLWeb uses to serve a conversational endpoint that AI agents can query directly rather than scraping HTML. Because it builds on schema.org markup, sitemaps and feeds you already maintain, it is incremental rather than a rebuild, and it moves the brand from being read by agents to being queryable by them.

suggested_action.summary: Evaluate an NLWeb instance exposing an /ask and /mcp endpoint over existing content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Point an NLWeb instance at your existing schema.org data and sitemap, and expose /ask and /mcp. Start with the content an agent is most likely to be asked about -- catalogue, docs, pricing.
